question.text: Lotus Growth AIF's Investment Manager, Mr. Ramesh Iyer, is preparing the data room for a USD 50 million institutional LP (a European pension fund) conducting investor due diligence. In the AIF context, 'Fund Due Diligence' by investors is BEST described as:

answer.text: The compliance audit conducted by SEBI on the Investment Manager every financial year.
The due diligence conducted by the Investment Manager on prospective portfolio/investee companies before making investments.
The process of investigation and evaluation performed by investors into the details of a potential AIF investment, including operations, management and verification of material facts.
The statutory audit of the fund's financial statements conducted by the external auditor.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 12, Fund Due Diligence is 'the process of investigation and evaluation, performed by investors, into the details of a potential investment, such as an examination of operations and management and the verification of material facts'. Because AIFs are privately placed and not all information is publicly available, investors are expected to conduct their own DD. The Trap: Option A confuses investor DD with a SEBI inspection; option B is investment-level DD on investee companies, not investor DD on the fund; option D is the statutory audit, which has a different purpose and audience. Note: Investor DD is investor-driven and fund-level; deal-level DD on investee companies and SEBI/statutory audits are separate processes.
